title: Lost in Berlin
tagline: Day one, zero German, a dead phone. Get Maya to her new flat.

beats.text: Listeners — if anyone is listening — this is it. Berlin. 7 a.m., one suitcase, zero German, and my phone just died at the gate. New plan: the podcast starts NOW, on this little recorder. And every podcast needs a sidekick. You. Yes, you.
beats.direction: Breathless, just off the plane, whispering into the recorder at an airport gate; the last three words are a grin.

beats.title: The survival page
beats.intro: No phone, but my guidebook has a survival page. Seven words. Tap the speaker to hear them — I'll only butcher them.

beats.question: Maya holds out the recorder. “Last line in my guidebook: ‘Hilfst du mir?’ — will you help me? Answer me in German.”

options.reply: “JA! My first German word is a YES. Partner, welcome to Kiez Krimi — episode zero.”
“I heard the no. I'm choosing to ignore the no. Try the other one.”
“Hallo to you too! But I asked if you'll HELP. Yes or no — and I need the yes.”

lines.text: A man with a coffee is walking right at me. He's SMILING. He's going to say something…

lines.name: A man with a coffee
lines.en: Good morning!

choose.reply: “NEIN?! He said good morning and I said NO. He looks wounded. Again!”
“Sorry for… what? He just said good morning. Say it back.”

lines.name: A man with a coffee
lines.en: Welcome to Berlin!
lines.direction: Warm, amused, like welcoming a lost tourist.

choose.reply: “So close. ‘Bitte’ is what HE says after my thank-you. I go first.”
“We did good morning. He said WELCOME. What do you say to a welcome?”

beats.reveal: Two lines. Two CORRECT lines. My first German conversation, listeners, and it was flawless.

beats.alt: Three hanging signs in the arrivals hall
beats.prompt: We need a train. Which sign? (The little pictures are your friends.)

spots.label: 👋 Willkommen
spots.miss: Willkommen is lovely — but it's a welcome, not a direction.

spots.label: Ausgang 🚶➜
spots.miss: Ausgang — the way OUT. To the taxis and their prices. No.

beats.reveal: Bahnhof — the station! Into the notebook, with its two neighbours. Airport train first, then the U-Bahn.

beats.text: Berlin weather, fun fact: it changes in ten seconds. We stepped outside, the sky opened, and my flatmate's note with the address… the ink RAN. Help me rebuild it. And the U-Bahn stop on it? I'm not saying it out loud. That's on you, partner.

beats.title: What's left on the note
beats.intro: Half of it ran. These words I can still make out — file them, then help me fill the holes.

beats.prompt: Dab the note dry: put each smudged word back where it belongs.

quiz.passage:
{1} Maya!
{2} in Berlin!
Die {3} ist in der {pool:streetSmudge} {pool:house}.
U-Bahn: {pool:station}.
{4}
Jonas

beats.text: Airport train, then the U-Bahn — yellow, fast, and it TALKS: before every stop a voice announces the next one. Podcast fact while we ride: see that needle with the disco ball? Berlin's TV tower. 368 metres, the tallest thing in Germany. Locals use it to find their way.
beats.direction: Excited tourist energy on the train, then the fun fact delivered with mock-seriousness.

beats.alt: The city passing the U-Bahn window
beats.prompt: For the notebook: which one is der Fernsehturm — the TV tower? Hint: disco ball.

spots.miss: That's a roof. A lovely roof. The tower is the NEEDLE.
Another roof! Berlin has a lot of those. Look UP.

beats.reveal: Der Fernsehturm. If we ever get lost: find the disco ball.

beats.speaker: announcer
beats.prompt: Every stop: ‘Nächster Halt’ — next stop — and a name. Some names sound ALIKE. Get Maya off at the stop from the note.
beats.wrongExitLine: Wrong platform! Back on, back on — Entschuldigung, Entschuldigung —
beats.missedLine: Wait. Was that OURS? The doors closed. We're going round again…
beats.reveal: {pool:station}! We're OFF. Partner, you have the ears of a bat. A helpful, German-speaking bat.

beats.title: Map words
beats.intro: A city map! On a board, like it's 1995. I can't read a word of it — but you can. The little pictures first, in German.

entries.en: here — Sie sind hier = you are here

beats.prompt: Podcast fact: Berlin has more bridges than VENICE. The city that is basically all bridges! Prove it — wo ist die Brücke?
beats.missLine: No water there. A bridge goes over the river.
beats.reveal: Die Brücke. Berlin, out-bridging Venice. That's going in the episode.

beats.prompt: First things first: Sie sind hier — you are here. Tap where WE are.
beats.missLine: We came up out of the U-Bahn. Find the square with the U.
beats.reveal: Hier. The square, by the U-Bahn. Everything starts from here.

beats.prompt: Now the big one. The note says ‘{pool:streetSmudge}’ — and some streets here start with the same letter. Read carefully: which one fits?
beats.missLine: Close, but read the END of the word on the note: ‘{pool:streetSmudge}’.
beats.reveal: {pool:street}! It fits, letter by letter — and the note said number {pool:house}. Clue secured: the address. Problem: this board shows WHERE, not which way to walk, and I can't carry a two-metre board. Time to ask a local.

chapters.title: Die Passantin
chapters.subtitle: the passer-by · which way?
chapters.lockedText: find the street on the map first

beats.text: A woman with a sausage dog, walking FAST. Locals always walk fast. We know the address — now I need the way, and she looks like she knows it. If she talks too fast, there are words for that.

beats.title: When they talk too fast
beats.intro: Survival German, part two. Honestly the most useful page in this notebook.

lines.en: Stop her politely: “Excuse me, where is {pool:street}?”

lines.name: The woman with the dog
lines.de: Die {pool:street}? Ach, das ist ganz einfach: {pool:way}, und dann sind Sie schon da!
lines.en: {pool:street}? Oh, that's easy: … and then you're there!
lines.direction: Very fast, in one breath, the way a local rattles off directions without slowing down for a tourist.

lines.text: That was… a LOT of words. At SPEED.

choose.reply: “We can't LEAVE — we caught nothing! Ask her to say it again.”
“Ja ja?! We nodded like we got it. We did NOT get it.”

lines.name: The woman with the dog
lines.de: Die {pool:street}? Ach, das ist ganz einfach: {pool:way}, und dann sind Sie schon da!
lines.direction: Very fast, in one breath, the way a local rattles off directions without slowing down for a tourist.

lines.text: Same speed. The SAME. Okay — honesty time.

choose.text: Ich verstehe nicht. Sprechen Sie Englisch?

choose.reply: “A third time at the same speed won't help. Tell her we don't understand — and try English.”
“See you soon?! We just MET her.”

lines.name: The woman with the dog
lines.de: Englisch? Nein, leider nicht. Aber ich sag's noch mal — ganz langsam.
lines.en: English? No, sorry. But I'll say it again — really slowly.
lines.direction: Apologetic at first, then kind and patient.

beats.reveal: She's going to say it again — slowly, pointing. Direction words are in the notebook. Ears on, partner.

lines.name: The woman with the dog
lines.en: So: {pool:street} — …
lines.direction: Slowly and very clearly, one chunk at a time, with a pause at the dash, like explaining to someone who barely speaks German.

lines.text: She's pointing. Trace her finger — which way first, and then?

lines.en: Trace the way she said, in order:

choose.reply: “No need — we GOT it this time! Thank her.”
“NEIN?! She just saved our whole afternoon!”

lines.name: The woman with the dog
lines.en: You're welcome! Bye!

choose.reply: “Hallo is hello — and she's LEAVING. Wave her off.”
“It's the afternoon, and she's GOING. The other goodbye word.”

beats.reveal: And she's gone, at full speed, the dog flying behind her like a little flag. Legend.

beats.alt: The pedestrian traffic light at the crossing
beats.prompt: Before we cross: tap the little man who says GO.

spots.miss: That's the red one — he says STOP. A grandma just tutted at us.

beats.reveal: That's das Ampelmännchen — Berlin's traffic-light man. The real ones wear a little HAT; he's from old East Berlin and people loved him so much he survived reunification. Also: Germans wait at red, even at 3 a.m. with no car in sight. Berliners… less famously. We wait.

beats.text: A bakery. Warm, smells like heaven, and the baker looks like she knows everyone on this street. Bakers know EVERYTHING — it's a law. Let's say hello properly and buy the famous Berlin doughnut. Bribery works in every language.

beats.title: Counter German
beats.intro: Bakery words. My guidebook says Berlin is FAMOUS for one thing: the Berliner, a jam doughnut. Obviously I am ordering one.

entries.en: the jam doughnut (what most of Germany calls it)

lines.text: Sun pouring through the window, lunch rush just over — the middle of the day. I go first: greet her for the time of day.

choose.reply: “It's half past two, partner. Morning was the airport — a lifetime ago.”
“See you soon? We just walked IN.”

lines.name: Frau Demir
lines.en: Hello! What can I get you?

lines.text: Order. The famous one. I have been waiting my whole flight for this.

lines.en: “A Berliner, please.”

lines.name: Frau Demir
lines.de: Einen Berliner? Ha! Hier in Berlin heißt das Pfannkuchen.
lines.en: A Berliner? Ha! Here in Berlin it’s called a Pfannkuchen.

entries.en: the jam doughnut (what Berliners call it)

lines.direction: Amused, teasing, a little laugh on "Ha".

lines.text: Podcast fact, LIVE: the rest of Germany calls it a Berliner. Berliners call it a Pfannkuchen. Berliners don’t call them Berliners. Okay. Again — the local way.

lines.en: “A Pfannkuchen, please.”

lines.name: Frau Demir
lines.en: Sure! Here you go.

beats.title: Who are you?
beats.intro: She's chatty. She's going to ask who I am. Notebook — fast!

lines.name: Frau Demir
lines.en: What's your name?

lines.name: Frau Demir
lines.de: Maya! Ich bin Frau Demir. Und Sie kommen aus…?
lines.en: Maya! I'm Mrs Demir. And you come from…?

lines.name: Frau Demir
lines.de: Amerika! Willkommen in Berlin! Und — wie geht's? Alles gut?
lines.en: America! Welcome to Berlin! And — how's it going? All good?

choose.reply: “Honest, but… we have a PRETZEL now. We're good.”
“She told us already — Frau Demir! She asked how we ARE.”

lines.text: NOW. The note. I hold it up, point at ‘Jonas’, and do my most hopeful face.

choose.reply: “Thanks for… Jonas? We haven't even found him. The polite opener is ‘excuse me’.”
“Close — but we're interrupting her day. The opener is ‘excuse me’.”

lines.name: Frau Demir
lines.de: Jonas? Ach, Jonas Weber! Ja, ja. Jeden Morgen: ein Pfannkuchen, ein Kaffee.
lines.en: Jonas? Oh, Jonas Weber! Yes, yes. Every morning: a Pfannkuchen, a coffee.
lines.direction: Delighted recognition, then fond, like describing a regular.

lines.text: Jonas WHO? She just said his surname. Which word was it?

choose.reply: “That’s his BREAKFAST, not his name.”
“That's WHEN he eats it. His name was the other word.”

beats.reveal: WEBER. That’s the name on the doorbell. And a Pfannkuchen and a coffee every morning — a man of taste…

beats.alt: The bakery counter: pretzels, doughnuts and coffee
beats.prompt: Frau Demir is pouring a coffee for Jonas — on the house! Tap what Jonas DRINKS every morning, so she knows I mean it.

spots.miss: A pretzel? Jonas is a Pfannkuchen man. And we want what he DRINKS.
That’s what he EATS — and I already have one. He drinks the other thing.

beats.reveal: Ein Kaffee for Jonas, to go — on the house. Frau Demir, I would die for you.

lines.text: Coffee for Jonas in one hand, Pfannkuchen in the other. Out we go — with the formal goodbye. Notebook, one more:

choose.reply: “That's hello. We're LEAVING.”
“We did that! The goodbye, partner.”

lines.name: Frau Demir
lines.en: Bye, Maya! See you soon!

beats.reveal: ‘Auf Wiedersehen’ from us, ‘Tschüss’ from her — both perfectly fine. Clue secured: the name on the bell.

beats.text: Street, way, name. Golden hour already — my suitcase has seen more of Berlin today than most tourists. Partner, the woman with the dog told us the way, and I can't read my own scribbles. You remember. You steer.

beats.prompt: We're on the Platz, facing the Fernsehturm — the disco ball. Wo ist die {pool:street}? Steer me, one corner at a time.
beats.bumpLine: Wrong turn! That's not what she said. Links, rechts, geradeaus — think back.
beats.reveal: {pool:street}! We WALKED here. In German. My feet hurt in German.

beats.alt: Three front doors with number plates
beats.prompt: {pool:street}. Three doors. Das Haus — the house — but which Nummer (number) was on the soaked note? No peeking.

spots.label: {pool:house:other1}
spots.miss: Nummer {pool:house:other1}? A man in a bathrobe is glaring at me through the window.

spots.label: {pool:house:other2}
spots.miss: Nummer {pool:house:other2}? There is a very small, very loud dog behind this one. No.

beats.reveal: Nummer {pool:house}. Das Haus! Our door. Probably. Let's find the bell.

beats.alt: A brass doorbell panel with name plates
beats.prompt: Haus Nummer {pool:house}. Four bells — three names, and der Hausmeister (the caretaker). One is Jonas. Ring it!

spots.label: Wagner
spots.miss: Wagner? Never heard of a Wagner. The baker said a different name…

spots.label: Becker
spots.miss: Becker — that sounds like ‘baker’, but it's not HIS name. What did Frau Demir say?

spots.label: Hausmeister
spots.miss: That's the Hausmeister — the caretaker. Jonas first: what was his surname?

beats.reveal: Ding… dong… nothing. NOTHING. He's not home. Of course he's not home.

lines.text: Wait — the door's opening. Someone's coming OUT. Look at the sky — and greet her first.

choose.reply: “Look at that sky, partner — it's EVENING.”
“The street lamps are ON. Day is over. The evening one.”

lines.name: A woman in a terracotta coat
lines.en: Good evening.

lines.text: Terracotta coat. Low bun. She glanced at the bells — at WEBER — then at me. Then walked off. And the door clicked shut behind her. Of COURSE.

beats.reveal: Who WAS that? No. Focus. One more bell has a word I can read: der Hausmeister — the caretaker.

lines.text: Ding-dong. Crackle. Somebody grumpy breathes into the intercom.

lines.name: The intercom
lines.en: Yes?
Greet him for the time of day, say who you are — and whose flat.

lines.name: The intercom
lines.de: Maya? … Ach so, zu Weber. Ja, ja. Kommen Sie rein.
lines.en: Maya? … Oh, right — for Weber's. Yes, yes. Come in.
lines.direction: Grumbling; a real pause at the ellipsis before the penny drops on "Ach so", then resigned.

lines.text: BZZZT. The door buzzes open. A grumpy, wonderful buzz.

beats.reveal: We're IN.

beats.text: On the stairs: a man in a flat cap with about a thousand keys. He hands me one, grumbles about having no TIME, and stomps off. Herr Böhm, the caretaker. I like him. I think.
beats.direction: Low and conspiratorial about the caretaker, affectionate on "I like him. I think."

beats.alt: A dark shared-flat kitchen with a note on the table
beats.note:
Hallo Maya!
Willkommen!
Hier ist Kaffee.
Bis bald!
Jonas
beats.prompt: The flat. Dark, warm, no Jonas — but a note on the table. Read it, then find what he left me.

spots.miss: A plant. Nice — but the note said Kaffee.
Just papers. The note says: hier ist KAFFEE.
Mugs! But… TWO? Wait. First the coffee he left me.
Mugs! But… TWO? Wait. First the coffee he left me.

beats.reveal: Kaffee! He left me a whole pot. We are SOULMATES.

beats.prompt: Wait. Two mugs on the table. I haven't touched either. Jonas isn't home. Look closely — what's wrong?

spots.miss: That one is cold. Look at the OTHER mug — closely.
The coffee pot is innocent. Look at the mugs.

beats.reveal: This one is still WARM. I put Frau Demir's coffee for Jonas down next to it — and it hit me: somebody was HERE. Ten minutes ago.

beats.question: Detective moment, partner. A warm mug, nobody home. Who had coffee here?

options.text: The woman in the terracotta coat
options.reply: “She came OUT of this building. She looked at WEBER. Partner… that’s episode one.”
“Then where IS he? Nobody answered his bell. Try again.”
“Böhm? He has NO TIME. For coffee least of all. Try again.”

beats.question: Okay. Deep breath. Sign off the episode for me — in German, to the listeners.

options.reply: “Tschüss — bis bald! Perfect. Partner, you just closed your first episode.”
“It's dark out. And we're saying GOODBYE.”

hub.title: {pool:station}. Three clues into the flat.
hub.lockedHint: The street, the way there, and the name on the bell — then we go.
hub.finaleLabel: Street, way, name → to the door
hub.allCluesLine: “Street, way, name. THAT’S ALL THREE. Partner — let’s go ring a doorbell.”

microChecks.text: someone just held the airport door for me. quick, what do I say?
microChecks.question: A stranger holds the door for Maya. She says…

microChecks.text: no peeking at the note: our U-Bahn stop. I'm NOT getting this wrong in front of the whole train.
microChecks.question: The stop on the note was…

microChecks.text: tomorrow, 8 a.m., Frau Demir waves at me through the window. what do I call out?
microChecks.question: At 8 in the morning Maya calls out…

ending.title: Case closed. Case… open?
ending.text: This was Kiez Krimi, episode zero. Maya is in — but Jonas isn't home, a woman in a terracotta coat looked at his bell, and somebody drank coffee in his kitchen. To crack what comes next, Maya needs more German: numbers, names, a few verbs. Learn them, and Episode 1 opens halfway through A1.1.
ending.line: “Day one in Berlin: SURVIVED. Best assistant a podcast ever had.”
